overview: Huntington Bancshares is a ~$280-290 billion regional bank holding company headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, whose principal subsidiary, The Huntington National Bank, provides full-service consumer and commercial banking across 21 states. Following the February 2026 all-stock merger with Cadence Bank and the late-2025 acquisition of Veritex Holdings, Huntington's historically Midwest-centric footprint (Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana, West Virginia, Minnesota) now extends deep into Texas and the Southeast (Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, Florida, Louisiana, Tennessee). The bank offers deposit, lending, payments, wealth management, capital markets, insurance and vehicle finance services, and has long differentiated its retail franchise through consumer-friendly features (24-Hour Grace, Fair Play Banking) and a #1 SBA 7(a) lending position.

business_model.summary: Huntington earns the large majority of revenue as net interest income from gathering low-cost core deposits and deploying them into consumer, commercial, and vehicle-finance loans, supplemented by fee income from payments, wealth/asset management, capital markets and insurance. The Cadence and Veritex deals roughly doubled the balance sheet's incremental scale versus the pre-merger Midwest franchise, but post-merger quarters (Q2-Q3 2026) have shown decelerating loan growth, flat-to-declining fee income, and rising credit costs as the combined book normalizes.

revenue_streams.name: Net interest income (loans/deposits spread)
revenue_streams.trend: growing but decelerating; NIM roughly flat ~3.25% in Q3 2026

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2C and B2B: consumer/retail banking, small business (SBA #1 lender by loan count for 15+ consecutive years), middle-market and large commercial, and vehicle dealer financing
business_model.geographic_mix: Historically concentrated in Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana, West Virginia and Minnesota; now expanded into Texas (Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston), Mississippi, and the broader Southeast via Cadence and Veritex, spanning 21 states post-merger; ~$284B total assets as of mid-2026

competitive_position.market_position: Top-10 U.S. regional/super-regional bank holding company by assets (~$284-290B) after the Cadence and Veritex deals; #1 SBA 7(a) lender by loan volume; leading bank in Mississippi by deposit share; 8th-largest bank in Texas; strong Midwest deposit franchise now supplemented by a growing Texas/South presence

moat_factors.description: Long-standing low-cost retail and commercial deposit relationships in Midwest markets provide funding cost advantages, though a deposit beta of 50-60% in the current cycle (above the ~45% seen in the prior cycle) is eroding this advantage faster than management originally modeled
15+ consecutive years as #1 SBA 7(a) lender by number of loans builds durable small-business relationships and cross-sell opportunities

Consumer-friendly features like 24-Hour Grace overdraft protection and Fair Play Banking commitments support customer retention and low attrition in retail banking; brand equity is strongest in the Great Lakes market and weaker in consumer savings/investment products

Cadence and Veritex acquisitions materially increased scale and commercial banking capacity, improving operating leverage and market power in new geographies, though integration-driven credit and fee softness in 2026 has partly offset the near-term benefit

Retail and commercial banking relationships (payroll, treasury services, deposit accounts) carry moderate switching costs typical of the banking industry; new Intelligent Treasury platform (launched with fintech Kyriba, November 2026) aims to deepen commercial treasury stickiness

weaknesses: Regional bank without the scale, diversification, or trading/investment-banking revenue of money-center banks (JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi)
Net interest margin highly sensitive to Fed policy and deposit competition, unlike more fee-diversified peers
Integration risk from back-to-back large acquisitions (Cadence, Veritex) still working through the loan book in 2026, with nonperforming assets up sharply ($1.72B at Q3 2026 vs. $821M a year earlier)
Explicit competitive pressure from well-capitalized FinTech companies cited in the FY2025 10-K
Commercial real estate exposure remains a sector-wide overhang for regional banks
Fee income momentum has stalled (down ~8% QoQ in Q3 2026) just as spread-income growth decelerates

growth_drivers: Cadence Bank merger (closed Feb 2026) and Veritex Holdings acquisition (closed late 2025) expanding Texas and Southeast commercial banking footprint and deposit base to 21 states
Fee income diversification via payments, wealth/asset management, and capital markets to reduce reliance on spread income (though momentum stalled in Q3 2026)
Continued small-business/SBA lending leadership driving new relationship acquisition and cross-sell
New commercial treasury platform (Intelligent Treasury, launched with Kyriba, November 2026) targeting multi-bank corporate clients
Share repurchases (at least $550 million in FY2026, with management signaling a $1.1-1.2 billion authorization sought for 2027) supporting EPS growth and capital return
Targeted operating leverage improvement toward a mid-to-low 54% efficiency ratio as Cadence/Veritex integration cost synergies are realized
2027 EPS target of growth of more than 20% versus 2025, with ROTCE rising into the 17-18% range
Vehicle finance and private wealth management as differentiated growth verticals versus Midwest peers

business.description: Systems conversions for Cadence (mid-2026) and Veritex (Q1 2026) are complete, but credit, fee and growth metrics in Q2-Q3 2026 show the combined franchise still normalizing, with slower organic loan growth (~6% full-year, down from earlier guidance) and declining fee income

Intense competition from PNC, Fifth Third, KeyCorp, Regions and national/money-center banks for deposits, commercial relationships, and digital banking share in overlapping Midwest and new Southern markets; FinTechs are an explicit competitive threat per the 10-K

business.risk: Deposit cost pressure / higher deposit beta
business.description: Management now models a 50-60% deposit beta versus ~45% in the prior cycle, directly compressing margin expansion and underpinning the lowered 2027 targets

business.risk: Credit normalization on an expanded loan book
business.description: Q3 2026 net charge-offs rose to ~0.31% of average loans (from 0.22% a year earlier) and nonperforming assets more than doubled YoY to $1.72B, driven partly by an idiosyncratic commercial credit but also broader nonaccrual growth across business, CRE and mortgage lending

financial.description: NIM was 3.25% in Q3 2026 (up modestly QoQ) but management guides Q4 2026 to roughly flat, and the higher deposit-beta assumption has pushed out the timeline for meaningful margin expansion

Management cut 2027 EPS guidance from $1.90-$1.93 to $1.75-$1.83 and lowered the 2027 ROTCE target from 18-19% to 17-18%, first flagged in September 2026 and reaffirmed (at the lower level) on the Q3 2026 call

CET1 ratio of ~10.0-10.1% and TCE ratio around 7% as of mid/late-2026 are adequate but were diluted by large stock-funded acquisitions; further deals or credit deterioration could pressure capital buffers

financial.risk: Credit costs on a rapidly grown, less-seasoned loan book
financial.description: Average loans grew sharply YoY on an acquisition-driven basis in 2026; full-year net charge-off guidance of 25-35bps is now running toward the upper half of that range

regulatory.description: Back-to-back large acquisitions increase regulatory (OCC/Fed) oversight of capital adequacy, CRA compliance, and systemic risk designation thresholds as HBAN approaches larger asset tiers; Huntington expanded its Washington, D.C. government/regulatory relations office in August 2026

Elevated capital, liquidity, and stress-testing requirements for regional banks following the 2023 regional bank crisis (SVB, Signature, First Republic) remain a compliance cost overhang for the sector
Overdraft/fee practices (e.g., 24-Hour Grace) and consumer protection regulation (CFPB) could evolve and affect fee income structures

macro.description: The Fed's September 2026 rate hike (first since 2023) directly triggered HBAN's initial guidance cut on NII and margin; further hikes or a higher-for-longer environment would keep pressuring deposit costs and loan demand

macro.risk: Commercial real estate maturity wall / credit normalization
macro.description: A large wall of U.S. CRE debt maturities continues through 2026-2027, with regional/community banks disproportionately exposed; HBAN's Q3 2026 nonaccrual growth spanned CRE alongside business and mortgage credit

As a regional lender with significant consumer and small-business exposure, HBAN's credit quality and loan demand are sensitive to broader economic deceleration; CEO Steve Steinour has publicly flagged market turbulence as a cause for concern

Competition from money-market funds and higher-yielding alternatives pressures banks to raise deposit rates, compressing net interest margin sector-wide and underpinning the elevated deposit-beta assumption

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Regional banking sector remains stable post-2023 crisis but is facing renewed margin pressure through 2026 as the Fed resumed rate hikes and deposit betas have run higher than the prior cycle; credit normalization is broadening beyond CRE office into general commercial and consumer books at several regional banks, while capital markets activity, M&A-driven scale, and eventual rate-cut tailwinds are partial offsets
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — bank earnings are sensitive to interest rate cycles, credit cycles, and economic growth; HBAN's consumer, small-business, and CRE exposure make it more cyclical than fee-heavy diversified financials
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — net interest income and margin are directly affected by Fed policy and deposit repricing behavior; HBAN's 2026 guidance cuts were explicitly tied to Fed policy and a higher-than-modeled deposit beta

recent_developments.event: Launched Intelligent Treasury, a modern treasury management platform for commercial clients built with fintech partner Kyriba, aimed at simplifying multi-bank liquidity management; Argus Research trimmed its price target from $20 to $18 (keeping a Buy rating) on November 5

Reported Q3 2026 results: GAAP EPS of $0.33 (adjusted $0.38, in line with consensus); revenue rose ~31% YoY to ~$2.81B on an acquisition-inflated basis; NIM ticked up to 3.25%; noninterest income fell ~8% QoQ; net charge-offs rose to 0.31% of average loans and nonperforming assets more than doubled YoY to $1.72B; management reaffirmed the lowered 2027 EPS target of $1.75-$1.83 (down from a prior $1.90-$1.93) and cut the 2027 ROTCE goal to 17-18% (from 18-19%), citing a higher deposit beta (50-60% vs. ~45% in the prior cycle); shares traded roughly flat on the print but several analysts (Wells Fargo, Argus, JPMorgan) kept price targets in the $18-21 range

Stock fell over 5% after management first cut 2027 EPS guidance from above $1.90 to $1.75-$1.83 and lowered 2026 NII growth guidance from 39-43% to roughly 35%, citing rising deposit costs and tightening loan pricing following the Fed's first rate hike since 2023; DA Davidson, Jefferies, Wells Fargo, and Evercore ISI subsequently cut price targets

Hired Laricke Blanchard to lead an expanded Washington, D.C. government and congressional/regulatory relations office, reflecting heightened regulatory engagement as the bank's asset size grows past $280B

Reported Q2 2026 results: net income of $727M ($0.33/share GAAP, $0.39 adjusted), NII up 40% YoY and 9% QoQ, noninterest income up 67% YoY to $785M, average loans up 42% YoY to $189.3B — all substantially inflated by the Cadence and Veritex acquisitions; completed Cadence systems conversion in mid-June; repurchased $159M of shares; CET1 10.0%, TCE ratio 7.1%, tangible book value per share $9.65

Completed all-stock acquisition of Cadence Bank (~462 million HBAN shares issued, ~$8.1B deal value), creating a combined institution with ~$279-284B in assets; added three former Cadence directors to the board including Vice Chairman Dan Rollins; became the leading bank in Mississippi by deposit share and the 8th-largest bank in Texas
Completed the ~$1.7-1.9B acquisition of Dallas-based Veritex Holdings, deepening Huntington's commitment to Texas (Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston)

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Steve Steinour has acknowledged market turbulence as a cause for concern while pointing to commercial and industrial lending strength. On the Q3 2026 call, management reaffirmed the lowered 2027 targets ($1.75-$1.83 EPS, 17-18% ROTCE) and attributed the reset primarily to a higher deposit beta (50-60%) than experienced in the prior rate cycle, alongside a weaker near-term fee outlook, faster CRE runoff, and modestly softer credit quality. Management continues to frame the Cadence/Veritex integration as largely complete operationally (systems conversions finished) even as credit and growth metrics normalize.

bull_case: Cadence Bank and Veritex acquisitions substantially scaled the balance sheet (~$284-290B assets) and expanded Huntington into faster-growing Texas and Southeast markets, diversifying away from a mature Midwest footprint

Management still projects 2027 EPS growth of over 20% versus 2025 and rising ROTCE (17-18%), with continued share buybacks ($550M in 2026, a larger program signaled for 2027) supporting per-share value

#1 SBA 7(a) lender for 15+ consecutive years provides a durable small-business relationship engine, and new commercial treasury technology (Intelligent Treasury/Kyriba) deepens switching costs with corporate clients

Valuation has become more attractive after repeated 2026 guidance resets, with consensus analyst price targets ($18-22) still implying upside from depressed levels, and several analysts (Argus, JPMorgan) maintaining Buy/Overweight ratings
NIM stabilized and ticked up slightly in Q3 2026 (3.25%), suggesting the worst of the immediate repricing shock may be behind the combined franchise
bear_case: Management has now cut 2027 guidance twice in 2026 (EPS from $1.90-$1.93 to $1.75-$1.83; ROTCE from 18-19% to 17-18%), raising doubts about forecasting discipline and the durability of post-merger synergy targets

A structurally higher deposit beta (50-60% vs. ~45% in the prior cycle) signals more persistent margin pressure than management initially modeled, directly compressing the bank's primary earnings driver

Credit quality is normalizing unfavorably: Q3 2026 nonperforming assets more than doubled YoY to $1.72B and net charge-offs rose to 0.31%, running toward the top of full-year guidance, on a loan book still digesting two large, near-simultaneous acquisitions

Fee income momentum stalled (down ~8% QoQ in Q3 2026) just as loan growth decelerated to ~6% organic for the year, undercutting the diversification thesis management has used to justify the M&A strategy

Regional bank sector faces an ongoing commercial real estate maturity wall with regional/community banks disproportionately exposed, and analyst price-target trims (Argus to $18 in November 2026) reflect increasing caution despite a plurality of Buy ratings
